doc: $~Main kisi bhi @language ka koi bhi matn zaahir kar sakta hoon. Bas matn ko matn ke shuru aur aakhir ki nishaniyon ke darmiyan rakhein: \""\, \“”\, \„“\, \''\, \‘’\, \‹›\, \«»\, \「」\, ya \『』\.
Samajhne ke liye, in khoobsurat jumlon ko dekhein
\'Zindagi guzaarne ke sirf do tareeqe hain. Ek yeh ke jaise kuch bhi mojiza nahin. Doosra yeh ke jaise har cheez mojiza hai.'\
\'一日三秋'\
Bas yaad rakhein, agar aap mujhe kholte hain to band bhi karein, aur milti julti nishani istemaal karein. Warna mujhe pata nahin chalega ke aap apne alfaaz se farigh ho gaye hain.
\'salaam'/ur'hola'/es-MX\
Aap mujhe zubaanon ke saath bhi tag kar sakte hain, aur kayi tarjume bhi de sakte hain. Jo zubaanein abhi chuni gayi hain, main unhi mein se milti hui zubaan ke mutabiq chalunga.
Agar aap mujhe kisi aur @values ke saath banana chahte hain, to aap yeh kar sakte hain:
\"Here are some sums \1 + 2\, \2 + 3\, \3 + 4\"\
Dekhein maine un jama ko kitni khoobsurati se chalaya, aur @Text ke andar rakha?

Mera ek aakhri chhota sa raaz hai: kya aap jaante hain ke hum sab ka ek alag number hota hai? Yeh sach hai! Aap hamein @U/ likh kar aur hamara number likh kar bula sakte hain. Misal ke taur par, @FunctionDefinition 192 hai:
Dekhein @U/192 kaise @FunctionDefinition ban gaya? Main sunta hoon aap in numbers ko 'Unicode' kehte hain.
Baqi, @FunctionDefinition ne mere liye itne shandaar functions banaye hain ke main alfaaz ke saath har tarah ke kaam kar sakta hoon!

Harfon ke bade aur chhote roop sirf kuch likhaai ke nizaamon mein hote hain. Jin mein yeh nahin hote, jaise Japani ya Arabi, un ka matn badalta nahin.
Mera @language tag tay karta hai ke kis zubaan ke usool istemaal hon. Turki mein noqte wali aur bina noqte wali i hoti hai, aur sirf Turki likha hua matn unhein Turki tareeqe se bada karta hai:
